We listened to feedback, followed better practices, and improved overall quality. These events are why we are delivering now, but everything has been updated for the present. 
Templates now live inside the monorepo at github effectstream/effectstream under the `templates/` directory (branch `v-next-bun-start`), rather than the separate `paima-game-templates` repo. This gives templates direct access to the framework build tooling and keeps them in sync with the framework version.
Even though we have delivered with the EffectStream monorepo, the original Paima Engine code is available at https://github.com/PaimaStudios/paima-engine at master branch and the original game templates at https://github.com/PaimaStudios/paima-game-templates.

ms.report:
Intro
This milestone delivers the proposal's second template: a novel technology integration: a fiat-to-crypto payment rail wired into an EffectStream app, so players can buy in-game items with a credit card instead of already holding crypto. It is meaningfully. Any developer can clone the repo and stand up the same fiat-purchase flow for their own OnChain app on Cardano or other blockchain given the cross chain nature.

1. Video of the working integration (YouTube, 1:29):
https://youtu.be/64fY35Sgu6E

2. Code - template, open source on GitHub:
https://github.com/effectstream/payment-app

3. Documentation & Write Up - how to leverage the template, introduces the technology, explains the engineering work
https://effectstream.github.io/docs/blog/payment-app
https://github.com/effectstream/payment-app/blob/main/README.md

COMMENTS & NOTES
This milestone is delivered under EffectStream (formerly Paima Engine), following the merger of Paima Studios into the Midnight Foundation. The rebrand and the project's continued in-scope delivery across Cardano and Midnight are acknowledged by the Catalyst team under support ticket #9527
Cardano-first / multi-chain: This is fundamentally a Cardano deliverable. EffectStream is a Cardano-rooted multi-chain engine, and the template's app logic carries zero chain-specific code - the logic of the app state transition, the endpoints, are all chain-neutral. Retargeting the template at Cardano is a config + contract-package change, not an app-logic change
This demo is runnable locally following the simple steps on the readme.

BRIEF
This milestone delivers a new template: a novel technology integration with Farcaster, the decentralised social network. Farcaster Canvas is a collaborative pixel-painting game that ships as a Farcaster Mini App: users on Warpcast paint the same canvas in near real time, and when a canvas fills, anyone can fork it to their own timeline. It is meaningfully different from the other templates: the client surface is a social feed embed - no game client, no wallet extension - while the whole game runs through an EffectStream state machine sitting between a near-empty contract and the UI.
There is no game logic on-chain and none in the frontend; everything is decided by the state machine consuming events from a single L2 input. Built on EffectStream, the game logic is chain-neutral: this build settles on an EVM chain inside Warpcast, and the same state machine retargets to the Cardano ecosystem with a configuration change - the social surface and the settlement chain are independent choices. So this game is an example how we can make cross social experiences with Cardano.

LINKS TO REVIEW
1. Video - Farcaster Canvas Mini App demo.
https://youtu.be/NYjVmRQBbcU
It is important to explain that Farcaster is an EVM native social network, with this App we can now do cross-chain content that targets both Cardano and Farcaster users in a integrated experience. We want to provide the tech that allows to expand on existing user bases, allowing Cardano to tap into them.

ms.report:
UPDATE 2 - Camera-based AR added to the app
Thanks once again for the feedback!
We have merged into the main branch, and now the main readme reflects the complete project.
UPDATE - Camera-based AR added to the app
Following the last review ("please fix it by adding actual augmented reality to the app"), camera-based AR Game is now in the app itself, built with ARKit + RealityKit. From the ranking screen, "Tiro al Trofeo" opens the camera: plane detection anchors a virtual podium onto the real surface, with physics gameplay (timed rounds, two-tier scoring), person occlusion, and the top contributors' names riding the podium steps. The same AR scene renders the template's geolocated records as a living data map on the real floor - GPS and AR integrated together, anonymized data anchored on Cardano.
New dedicated AR demo video (on-device, single take): 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7qFVhvGDVyk

Code: https://github.com/effectstream/ipp-app - see ios/IPP/Game/(AR session, plane placement, procedural podium, physics toss, floor data map). The README note quoted in the review ("no ARKit/RealityKit overlay") has been removed - it is no longer true; that section now documents the camera AR feature, as discussed in previous reviews.

ms.report:
In response to the review of the PoA
Thank you for the review. The points raised are answered below.
1. The applications and games are listed further down with the template each one uses, how it is integrated, and a link, covering all five templates.
2. Why the earlier list read as M2-only. It named Catalyst projects that use the EVM-Cardano development environment. That environment is the shared foundation every other template runs on, so a list built that way collapses onto M2 even when the work spans all five. 
3. Use beyond our own team: The templates are open source, so uptake is normally by fork, no registration or communication is needed. As today the EffectStream monorepo carrying the templates has 91 stars and 43 forks, and the game-templates repository behind the M1 GameMaker integration, and M2, M3, M4 has further forks. We will report named third-party applications in the Effectstream home site. We just promoted the engine in a hackathon recently with very good reception.
4. The deliverables noted as missing. The M2 write-up and demonstration video, and the M5 write-up, are in the per-template sections below, which carry code, README, write-up and video for every milestone.
Milestone 5 was updated. The close-out video now includes the camera-based augmented reality added to the M5 template, and the close-out report carries the applications table and confirms M5's platform as iOS (ARKit and RealityKit).
